---
title: "Suggest an improvement"
---

Send one suggestion through the handbook's public GitHub form when something is missing, unclear, wrong or difficult to use. You do not need finished wording, and you will not be asked to edit the book.

[Suggest an improvement](https://github.com/hareshsuppiah/handbook-for-the-recently-enrolled/issues/new?template=share-feedback.yml){.btn .btn-primary}

The form requires a free GitHub account. GitHub calls your suggestion an **issue**. For this handbook, an issue is the public record of your suggestion and the editor's response.

## Use the form for

Use the same form to:

- add a missing question, topic, checklist, template or example;
- correct or clarify advice;
- shorten, combine or remove material;
- share a useful source or example;
- report a reading, navigation, accessibility or technical problem; or
- explain where advice needs a clearer institutional, disciplinary, methodological or jurisdictional limit.

Send one distinct suggestion at a time. This lets the editor discuss and decide each change on its own merits.

## Before you open the form

GitHub submissions are public. Remove personal information, participant data, private correspondence, complaints casework, confidential research, passwords, unpublished results and details that identify another person. Describe the general problem instead.

Do not use the form for a private, urgent or personal matter. See [Local rules and specialist help](../support.qmd) and use the appropriate local route.

## What happens next

1. An editor checks the suggestion for private information and looks for an existing suggestion or answer.
2. The editor may ask you a question or request a source.
3. The project lead accepts it for drafting, merges it with an existing suggestion, defers it or declines it.
4. A human contributor or AI agent may prepare a proposed change.
5. A human reviews the wording, evidence and relevant handbook checks.
6. The project lead publishes it, requests another revision or rejects the proposed change.

The first decision concerns the suggestion. Publication requires a separate review of the actual change.

## First time using GitHub?

Use the [first-time GitHub guide](how-to-help.qmd). It shows how to create an account, complete and preview the form, submit it, follow replies and update your suggestion. You can also read [what happens to a suggestion](editorial-workflow.qmd), [how AI assistance is used](ai-and-editorial-practice.qmd) and [how visuals and contributor credit are handled](visuals-and-credit.qmd).

## Credit

You can request credit under your GitHub username, your preferred name, an organisation or a pseudonym. You can also choose no public credit. A useful contribution can be credited even when the published wording differs from the suggestion.

## Follow existing suggestions

[Read the tracker guide](tracker.qmd) or [open the live GitHub issue tracker](https://github.com/hareshsuppiah/handbook-for-the-recently-enrolled/issues). Read the decision and linked edits; an approved suggestion is not yet a published change.
